data.title: A Miami Honeymoon Inspired One Couple to Build a Candy-Colored Home in London — WSJ
data.description:
By Ruth Bloomfield

Inspired by Miami's Art Deco architecture, the eccentric but charming Cloud House in north London took architect Peter Morris and his wife, Emily Kennedy, a decade to create.

With its marshmallow-pink exterior, turquoise-framed windows and the fluted roofline that inspired its name, the house cost them about $971,000 to build — nearly as much as the roughly $1.25 million that the couple had paid for the site in 2016.

Now, less than three months after moving in, the couple are listing the approximately 1,404-square-foot house in the neighborhood of Gospel Oak for GBP2.5 million, or about $3.3 million.

Morris, founder of Peter Morris Architects, and Kennedy, a television producer, are selling because they want a new house-building challenge, said Kennedy, who had renovated a half-dozen houses before Cloud House. "We knew we would not stay here forever," she said. "But it was beautiful to make this dream house."

The property initially came with a two-bedroom Victorian cottage and a backyard to the side, which Morris said he saw potential to redevelop.

The couple got married in 2017 and spent their honeymoon in Miami. "It was inspiring — all the beautiful curves on the buildings," said Morris. "The colors, the turquoise sea and the pink flamingos."

As soon as Morris returned to London, with Kennedy's encouragement, he started drawing up plans to replace the cottage with a pair of three-story houses.

It took the couple four years to persuade local planners to let them proceed with their unusual vision. To help finance the property, the couple listed one of the houses as a work-in-progress, offering the land, the plans and Morris's assistance in getting it built. A young East London-based family paid roughly $1.32 million for it. They will be moving in before Christmas.

Work finally began in 2023 with the demolition of the cottage. The design of the house was also inspired by other playful spaces, including traditional sweet shops, ice cream parlors and fairgrounds, Morris said.

The commitment to this theme goes beyond the exterior. The kitchen island is pink with green-and-white cabinet doors and yellow handles. Sections of the kitchen ceiling are candy-striped in pink and white, with beaded cornicing. The floor is mint green, and the doors leading to Morris's study, a guest bathroom and the staircase are cobalt blue.

Upstairs, the couple obliged the request of their 20-year-old daughter, Astha Morris, a college student who wanted a pink-and-red bathroom beside her bedroom.

One of the couple's favorite features is the roof terrace, enclosed by pink plaster walls. With views of a nearby Victorian church spire and neighboring buildings, it is fitted with a tub and seating.

The property has attracted so much attention that it was featured on the British TV series "Grand Designs," with presenter Kevin McCloud describing it as "one perfectly baked pink pudding."

For listing agent Becky Fatemi of United Kingdom Sotheby's International Realty, valuing the house was a challenge, but she said it commands a premium for the neighborhood, despite its relatively modest floor space. "You can look at all the comparables in Gospel Oak, but none of them will tell you what Cloud House is worth," she said.

data.title: Tech stocks tumble, Treasury yields fall as traders seek refuge
data.description:
Key points:
  • Ex-Japan Asian stocks post biggest weekly drop since COVID hit
  • Anthropic shares fall as much as 12.5%
  • US bonds rally, gold and silver at 2026 lows

By Rodrigo Campos and Harry Robertson

Tumbling technology-related shares led a global stock selloff on Friday, with US traders rotating into defensive sectors and the US 10-year yield dropping by the most in a month.

Stock benchmarks in Japan and Korea tumbled over 5% overnight to close the week, while on Wall Street chipmaker shares were down close to 6%. Taiwanese shares TWSE:TAIEX were down 17% for the week, their biggest weekly decline since 1990. Anthropic fell as much as 12.5% on its first full day of trading.

Consumer staples and healthcare led sector gains on the S&P 500, which was still on track to post its largest weekly loss since March 2025.

"Markets are entering a more defensive phase," said Daniela Hathorn, senior market analyst at Capital.com.

"Strong AI demand and successful individual listings are no longer sufficient to sustain broader risk appetite when investors are questioning valuations, borrowing costs and the outlook for corporate profitability."

The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.08% to 49,135.56, the S&P 500 CBOE:SPX fell 1.20% to 7,089.64 and the Nasdaq Composite fell 2.37% to 23,314.06.

MSCI's gauge of stocks across the globe EURONEXT:IACWI fell 1.60% and the pan-European STOXX 600 index fell 1.83%. Emerging market stocks CBOE:EFS fell 3.11%.

The MSCI index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan (.MISX00000PUS) tumbled 8.3% this week, its largest such drop since the COVID pandemic in March 2020.

The VIX index, linked to the cost of insurance against a drop on the S&P 500, traded at its highest since March .

As investors sought safe-haven assets, government bonds rallied.

The yield on benchmark US 10-year notes fell 10.43 basis points to 4.948% and the 30-year bond (US30YT=RR) yield fell 6.39 basis points to 5.3371%. The 10-year yield is on track to post its largest daily basis point drop since October 22.

The 2-year note (US2YT=RR) yield, which typically moves in step with interest rate expectations for the Federal Reserve, fell 12.57 basis points to 4.653% even as a rate hike is priced in for next month's policy meeting.

DOLLAR AND OIL DROP

The dollar index dipped after touching a 19-month high on Thursday. The dollar's recent rally has been fueled by bets on tighter monetary policy due to hotter-than-expected US inflation data.

"I think the momentum has stalled for the dollar ... but I think it's a little bit early to pick a top for the dollar," said Marc Chandler, chief market strategist at Bannockburn Capital Markets.

The dollar index fell 0.21% to 103.73, with the euro up 0.15% at $1.0982. Against the Japanese yen , the dollar weakened 0.62% to 158.7.

In commodities, crude prices fell on strong exports from the Middle East and reports of tanker disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz.

US crude fell 0.75% to $82.59 a barrel and Brent fell to $91.02 per barrel, down 1.04% on the day.

Spot gold fell 2.02% to $3,548.53 an ounce and spot silver fell 2.54% to $41.66 an ounce, both trading at their lowest since September 2025. Copper declined 2.71% to $12,186.00 a ton.

data.title: Canada Retail Sales Pull Back After 0.8% Rise in September — 2nd Update
data.description:
By Robb M. Stewart

OTTAWA--Canadian retail sales are heading for the sharpest drop in more than a year and a half, a possible sign of cracks in the resilience of household spending and slowing momentum for the economy.

The value of retail trade in the country increased 0.8% in September from the month before to a seasonally adjusted 75.31 billion Canadian dollars, the equivalent of about US$52.51 billion, Statistics Canada said Friday. That was a tick stronger than the 0.7% growth economists expected but was driven by a jump in how much drivers spent at the pumps.

An early tally of receipts indicates sales in October dropped 1.5%, which would be the steepest fall since February 2025.

Consumer spending in Canada remained solid through the third quarter, helping support economic growth. Retail sales rose 1.2% during the last quarter and volumes were up 1%, though sales volumes in September were up a slim 0.1%. The estimated weak start to the final quarter of 2026 could be even more pronounced in volume terms given seasonally-adjusted gasoline prices and goods prices generally were up slightly in October.

The Bank of Canada has projected economic growth will cool in the fourth quarter to below 1% annualized as the country adjusts to the latest U.S. tariffs, then recover next year. Economists say a string of soft data may point to even weaker growth, and undercut the case for further interest-rate increases near term.

"At this point, the likelihood of a hike in December is around 50-50, but diminishing," Charles St-Arnaud, chief economist at Servus Credit Union, said.

"Weakness in the economy in recent weeks suggests the Bank of Canada should pause to better assess the situation before hiking again, especially with some fuel prices easing recently," St-Arnaud said.

Statistics Canada provided no detail with its October estimate. The data agency's survey for September showed sales were up in five of the nine industry segments it tracks, led by trade at gas stations. Stripping out fuel, sales edged up 0.1 for the month.

Core sales, which strip out both fuel and motor vehicles and parts, similarly nudged up 0.1% for the month with a boost from general merchandise stores. Canadians also spent more on clothing, and on health and personal care but less at supermarkets and other grocery retailers.

"Once again, we're seeing a small uptick in Canadians' spending, but it hasn't really corresponded with them actually buying more," Jasleen Kaur Trehan, an economist at the Canadian Chamber of Commerce, said.

"September's retail numbers are again an example of how higher prices can make consumer spending look healthier than it really is," Kaur Trehan said. "With economic growth losing steam, a softer labor market and stubborn inflation squeezing purchasing power, households have less room to keep spending," she added.

The Bank of Canada's focus has turned to rising inflation risk, which prompted it to raise its policy interest rate in October for the first time in more than three years. Annual inflation has been at, or above, the upper end of the central bank's 1%-3% control range four months running, holding at 3.1% in October even as underlying measures of core inflation have remained more contained.

Statistics Canada's previous estimate of industry accounts suggested gross domestic product contracted 0.1% between August and September after essentially no change the previous two months, which would translate into annualized growth in the third quarter of 1.3% after a strong 3.8% expansion the quarter before. At the same time, employment in Canada has fallen three months running, driving the jobless rate in October to a six-month high of 6.7%.

"Today's data confirm that consumer spending will be a solid positive contributor to third-quarter GDP but also appear to signal that the slowing in growth seen late in the quarter and into the start of fourth quarter hasn't stemmed solely from sectors directly exposed to U.S. tariffs," Andrew Grantham, senior economist at CIBC Capital Markets, said.

Write to Robb M. Stewart at robb.stewart@wsj.com

data.title: IHCL opens Taj Yelahanka, Bengaluru, marking its 400th operating hotel
data.description:
Indian Hotels Company (IHCL) and Krishna GVK Luxury Hotels Ltd (formerly Taj GVK Hotels & Resorts Ltd) have announced the opening of Taj Yelahanka, Bengaluru, marking IHCL's 400th operating hotel.

Puneet Chhatwal, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, IHCL, said, “Taj Yelahanka, Bengaluru is the seventh hotel in our partnership with Krishna GVK Luxury Hotels and we are delighted that this opening also marks the milestone of IHCL’s 400th operating hotel. The 256-key Taj hotel expands our presence in North Bengaluru, a rapidly developing growth corridor, enabling us to capitalise on the robust demand in one of India's most dynamic lodging markets. We will continue to pursue opportunities with Krishna GVK in the luxury segment across key metros and established leisure destinations such as Goa, leveraging our complementary strengths in asset development and hotel operations through a capital-light management model.”

The 256-key property features rooms and suites set amid landscaped gardens. Its food and beverage portfolio includes Vista, an all-day dining restaurant; Nonya, offering Pan-Asian cuisine; and House of Nomad, a rooftop destination. The hotel also features the J Wellness Circle, a heated swimming pool and a fitness centre. It offers venues for conferences, celebrations and social occasions, catering to both business and leisure travellers.

Krishna Bhupal, Joint Managing Director, Krishna GVK Luxury Hotels Ltd, said, “Today marks the beginning of a new phase of growth for Krishna GVK. We have charted an ambitious growth trajectory, with a clear vision to scale beyond. Having built a strong legacy of developing some of India’s finest hotels in partnership with IHCL over the past 25 years, Taj Yelahanka, IHCL’s 400th hotel, marks an important milestone in our entry into Bengaluru.

As we look ahead, we are poised to accelerate our expansion across India’s leading metropolitan markets and high-potential leisure destinations, including Goa, strategically broadening our footprint and strengthening our presence in key growth markets. Our drive is not merely to expand our portfolio, but to build a strong, diversified hospitality presence across the country, taking our total inventory to 2,200 keys and beyond. Our balance sheet is strong, our net debt is minimal, and we are ready to pursue growth both organically and through strategic acquisitions.”

data.title: ITC Hotels unveils MS Dhoni Tribute Room at ITC Grand Chola, Chennai
data.description:
ITC Hotels has introduced the MS Dhoni Tribute Room at ITC Grand Chola, Chennai, an immersive hospitality experience celebrating the legacy of Indian cricket icon Mahendra Singh Dhoni. The experience brings together memorabilia, bespoke design, curated storytelling and personalised hospitality, highlighting his achievements and values of humility, resilience and excellence.

The tribute features an exclusive collection of jerseys, signed cricket memorabilia, gloves, stumps and commemorative trophies, showcasing defining moments from Dhoni's career. The specially designed room incorporates commissioned artwork and personalised amenities inspired by his iconic Number 7.

The experience also includes The Captain's Pantry, a culinary offering inspired by Dhoni's personal favourites and created by ITC Hotels' master chefs. For younger guests, curated experiences and keepsakes highlight perseverance, teamwork, leadership and sporting excellence. An exclusive audio-visual presentation traces Dhoni's journey from Ranchi to the pinnacle of world cricket.

Personalised in-room touches include custom-designed robes, towels, cushions and premium amenities featuring the iconic Number 7.

data.title: Naxatra Labs Appoints Former Ather Energy Executive Naveen Veeramaneni As Chief Product Officer
data.description:
The appointment will strengthen the company's product development, engineering and manufacturing capabilities as it expands its electric motor and propulsion technology business

Naxatra Labs has appointed Naveen Deepak Veeramaneni as its Chief Product Officer (CPO), bringing in a former Ather Energy engineering leader to strengthen its product development and manufacturing capabilities.

In his new role, Veeramaneni will oversee the company's Product, Engineering and Manufacturing functions. His responsibilities will include executing the product roadmap, strengthening engineering processes and developing scalable manufacturing systems.

Veeramaneni brings experience in electric motor engineering, powertrain development and product engineering. Before joining Naxatra Labs, he spent nearly five years at Ather Energy, where he led motor engineering and subsequently the E-Powertrain team. He has also worked with Varroc in motor design and holds a PhD in Electric Machines from IIT Gandhinagar.

At Naxatra Labs, Veeramaneni will focus on integrating product development, engineering and manufacturing operations. His mandate includes strengthening processes across product conceptualisation, prototyping, testing, validation and commercial-scale manufacturing.

The company also aims to improve manufacturing quality, production efficiency and product reliability while developing solutions tailored to specific customer and industry requirements.

Expanding Electric Motor Technology Applications

The appointment comes as electric motor and propulsion technologies find applications across electric mobility, agriculture, drones, robotics and industrial sectors.

Naxatra Labs is focusing on developing indigenous electric motor and propulsion technologies through in-house design, engineering, simulation, prototyping and testing capabilities.

Veeramaneni said he would focus on strengthening product development processes and manufacturing capabilities, with an emphasis on developing reliable, high-performance solutions for customers across industries.

The company aims to strengthen integration between its product, engineering and manufacturing functions as it builds application-specific technologies and prepares for manufacturing scale-up.

data.title: Robusta coffee hits 3-year low as Vietnam harvest ramps up
data.description:
Robusta coffee futures on the ICE exchange hit three-year lows on Friday, heading for 10% weekly falls as the harvest in top grower Vietnam ramps up.

Raw sugar also hit three-month lows.

COFFEE

* Robusta coffee fell 2.5% to $2,904 a metric ton at 1623 GMT, after setting a three-year low of $2,854.

* A Vietnam-based dealer noted that ICE futures have fallen sharply yet local price discounts for physical robusta are still easing. "That is the clearest sign so far of growing supply pressure," he said.

* Elsewhere, the recent weakness of Brazil's real currency has encouraged exports from the world's second largest robusta producer.

* Brazil's currency fell to its lowest level since April 2025 on Thursday.

* Arabica coffee fell 0.8% to $2.7375 per lb.

SUGAR

* Raw sugar fell 1.2% to 16.96 cents per lb after setting a three-month low of 16.82.

* Funds have been scaling back a net long position in raw sugar ahead of the year end, with the market looking technically bearish after breaking below key support levels.

* Physical sugar broker Deepcore noted some bearish fundamental factors also, namely, estimates of 13% growth in top grower Brazil's 2027 sugar output and limited interest in India's duty-free raw sugar import programme.

* White sugar lost 0.5% to $485.70 a metric ton.

COCOA

* London cocoa ​​rose 1.5% to £4,097 per ton.

* Low port arrivals in top grower Ivory Coast are helping underpin cocoa, as are estimate for sharply reduced 2026/27 output in Ecuador.

* Ample availability of cocoa from the 2025/26 crop, however, continued to keep a lid on prices.

* New York cocoa gained 1.5% to $5,277 a ton.

data.title: US yields drop as AI trade concern spurs safe-haven bid
data.description:
Key points:
  • Nasdaq down more than 2% early
  • Anthropic shares also decline
  • Worries about AI trade intensify

By Caroline Valetkevitch and Sophie Kiderlin

US Treasury yields fell on Friday, with the benchmark 10-year yield set for its biggest weekly drop since early April 2025, as worries about the AI trade weighed on equities and led investors to seek out safe-haven assets.

The yield on the 10-year Treasury note was back below 5% and on track for its biggest daily drop since October.

The Nasdaq was down more than 2% early as fears intensified over the AI trade despite Anthropic's blockbuster market debut on Thursday.

Anthropic shares were down more than 10% on Friday, while an index of semiconductors was down more than 7%. US stocks were also on track for a steep weekly fall.

Concerns about companies' rising spending and debt load related to AI, Jensen Huang's departure from Nvidia, and worries about tougher scrutiny and a deceleration of data-center expansion after the Democrats' midterm sweep have all weighed on investor sentiment in recent weeks.

"Because of the decline in equity prices and fears that the AI spend will moderate, you have a little bit of a growth fear in terms of the economy seeping into the markets," said Jim Awad, senior managing director at Clearstead Advisors LLC in New York.

That is forcing a decline in longer-dated bond yields, while shorter-dated Treasury yields are somewhat supported by expectations that the US Federal Reserve will raise interest rates in the coming months, he said.

Bond prices rise as yields fall.

Fed funds futures traders were last pricing in an almost 100% chance of a 25-basis-point hike at the US central bank's December 8 to 9 meeting, the CME Group's FedWatch Tool showed.

A larger, 50-basis-point increase has also been brought into the mix, although money market expectations for such a hike have been pared back.

Yields jumped last week after hawkish Fed official comments and hotter-than-expected US consumer price data.

The yield on the benchmark US 10-year Treasury note was down 10.8 basis points at 4.944% and was on track for its biggest weekly decline since early April 2025, when US President Donald Trump announced sweeping tariffs. The yield on the 30-year bond (US30YT=RR) was down 6.8 basis points at 5.333%.

The two-year (US2YT=RR) US Treasury yield, which typically moves in step with interest rate expectations for the Fed, was down 13.2 basis points at 4.647%.

A closely watched part of the US Treasury yield curve measuring the gap between yields on two- and 10-year Treasury notes (US2US10=TWEB), seen as an indicator of economic expectations, was at a positive 29.3 basis points.

The breakeven rate on five-year US Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities (TIPS) (US5YTIP=TWEB) was last at 2.175% after closing at 2.223% on Thursday.

The 10-year TIPS breakeven rate (US10YTIP=TWEB) was last at 2.149%, indicating the market sees inflation averaging about 2.1% a year for the next decade.

data.title: Scott Bessent Says Trump-Xi Talks Did Not Address Jensen Huang, Left Nvidia H200 Policy Unchanged
data.description:
Key points:
  • Bessent said the administration was also addressing remote access to computing power through overseas data centers.
  • According to him, limited demand from Chinese buyers, rather than a change in U.S. policy, explained Nvidia’s decision to stop shipping H200 chips to China. 
  • Nvidia’s market capitalization dropped below Alphabet on Friday.

Nvidia (NVDA) CEO Jensen Huang did not come up during discussions between President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Friday.

“No, not at all,” Bessent said in a CNBC interview Friday when asked whether Huang or the spy allegations surrounding Nvidia had been raised during the meeting.

Bessent also stated that the administration’s existing policy around chip exports remained unchanged, with the H200 representing the threshold level of chip technology that can be sold to Chinese buyers.

“I wouldn't anticipate any change in the policy,” Bessent said, adding that Trump had drawn a “very firm line” at the H200.

NVDA stock fell over 6% in morning trade on Friday, on track to hit a fresh 16-month low and mark a seven-day losing streak. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around Nvidia remained in ‘extremely bullish’ territory over the past day, accompanied by ‘extremely high’ levels of chatter.

Nvidia’s market capitalization also slipped below Alphabet’s during Friday’s trading session, pushing the chipmaker to fourth place among the most valuable U.S. companies.

Bessent Says China Has Placed Few Orders For H200 Chips

Bessent suggested that limited demand from Chinese buyers, rather than a change in U.S. policy, explained Nvidia’s decision to stop shipping H200 chips to China despite having U.S. licenses and approval to do so.

“I think what we have seen is a paucity of orders from the Chinese on the H200s as they try to build out their own chip stack,” he said. Bessent added that China was likely “many years behind” in developing its own semiconductor capabilities.

His comments follow Nvidia’s disclosure this week that it had stopped shipping H200 chips to China, despite receiving U.S. approval.

The Treasury secretary also addressed concerns about overseas data centers providing computing capacity to Chinese customers without physically shipping restricted chips into the country.

He said the administration was taking a “more common sense approach” to remote access, arguing that it made little sense to prohibit direct chip sales if Chinese companies could simply lease computing power from facilities abroad.

Bessent Says Administration Is Aligned On China Policy

“I think we're all committed to following President Trump's instructions,” Bessent said.

He added that the administration was working to ensure that appropriate chip restrictions were in place and that remote access to computing capacity had been curtailed.

He also said the U.S. was seeking to maintain its lead in semiconductor technology and artificial intelligence.

“We don't want to decouple. We just need to de-risk,” Bessent said, describing the administration's approach to the U.S.-China relationship.

Both leading ETFs covering semiconductors, the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) and the VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH), were down over 6% in morning trade on Friday. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around both trended in ‘bearish’ territory over the past day.

November 20 (Renewables Now) - Spanish utility Iberdrola SA has finalised the repowering of its Isabela and Molar del Molinar wind farms in the Castile-La Mancha region, maintaining their capacity at 97.5 MW with fewer turbines.

The two wind farms are more than two decades old and are some of the first that Iberdrola installed in Spain. Their repowering involved replacing 139 turbines with 22 new machines, which is expected to increase electricity production by around 30%, the utility said.

At the 49.5-MW Molar del Molinar wind farm in Penas de San Pedro, Iberdrola replaced 75 turbines rated at 660 kW each with 11 Vestas machines of 4.5 MW apiece.

At the 48-MW Isabela wind farm, near Casas de Lazaro and Penascosa, the company took down 64 turbines rated at 750 kW to add 11 new machines, six rated at 4.5 MW and five at 4.2 MW.

The two renovated wind farms are expected to generate enough electricity to meet the annual consumption of more than 55,500 households, Iberdrola said.

Construction at Isabel and Molar del Molinar began in 2024. The projects received a combined EUR 22.71 million (USD 24.9m) in support from the Spanish state under the Circular Repowering programme, managed by the Institute for Energy Diversification and Saving (IDAE).

During the works, Iberdrola hired EnergyLoop, a recycling company established by Iberdrola Ventures Perseo and FCC Ambito, to process the decommissioned turbine blades. The operation involved removing 139 turbines and 417 blades, with more than 800 tonnes of material treated for recovery and recycling.

(EUR 1.0 = USD 1.098)

data.title: S&P 500 Flirts With Correction — WSJ
data.description:
By WSJ Staff

The S&P 500 is down again today, putting it close to correction territory, generally defined as a 10% from a recent peak.

The level to watch for the broad stock benchmark is 7037.04. That wold be 10% below its Oct. 6 high. The index was recently trading at about about 7070.

  • If it enters a correction, the S&P would join the Nasdaq composite, which has been in correction since Nov. 5.
  • The Dow Jones Industrial Average isn't too far from correction territory, either: It will enter correction territory if it falls to 48914.21.

This item is part of a Wall Street Journal live coverage event. The full stream can be found by searching P/WSJL (WSJ Live Coverage).

data.title: REG - Ormonde Mining PLC - Issue of Equity
data.description:
RNS Number : 1303E Ormonde Mining PLC 20 November 2026  

20 November 2026

Ormonde Mining plc

(“Ormonde” or the “Company”)

Subscription for New Shares to Raise £71,500

Ormonde Mining plc (AQSE: ORM), the natural resources company with investment exposure to outstanding gold exploration assets, announces it has raised gross proceeds of £71,500 through a direct subscription (the “Subscription”) for 715,000 new ordinary shares of €0.0005 each in the Company (the “Subscription Shares”) at a price of 10 pence per share (the “Issue Price”). The Issue Price represents a premium of 11% to the closing mid-market price of 19 November 2026.

The Subscription has been made by Inspiration Holdings Limited (“IHL”), a company wholly owned by Thomas Anderson, the Company’s largest shareholder. Following Admission, Mr Anderson will be interested directly and indirectly in 3,077,000 ordinary shares, representing 29.98% of the Company’s enlarged issued share capital.

Use of Proceeds

The net proceeds will strengthen the Company’s working capital position and support ongoing work in respect of its Zamora licenses and wider opportunities in Spain.

Related Party Transaction

The Subscription constitutes a related party transaction under Rule 4.6 of the AQSE Growth Market Access Rulebook as Brendan McMorrow, Chief Executive Officer of the Company, is a director of IHL. Brian Timmons and Steve Nicol, being the independent directors for the purposes of this transaction, consider that having exercised reasonable care, skill and diligence, the related party transaction is fair and reasonable as far as the shareholders of Ormonde are concerned.

Admission and Total Voting Rights

Application has been made to for the Subscription Shares to be admitted to trading on the Aquis Stock Exchange Growth Market (“Admission”). Admission is expected to become effective, and dealings to commence, at 8.00 a.m. on or around 26 November 2026.

Following Admission, the Company’s issued share capital will comprise 10,265,150 Ordinary Shares, each with one voting right. The Company holds no shares in treasury. This figure may be used by shareholders as the denominator for the calculations by which they will determine whether they are required to notify their interest in, or a change to their interest in, the Company's share capital under the Disclosure Guidance and Transparency Rules.

SEDOL Code Update

Further to the Capital Reorganisation approved at the Extraordinary General Meeting of the Company held on 27 October 2026, Ormonde has been issued with a new SEDOL. The Company’s SEDOL is now BNZKXW8. As previously announced, the Company’s ISIN is IE000N7GHDG0.

data.title: KIMPTON SURFCOMBER HOTEL DEEPENS ITS CONNECTION TO THE ARTS WITH A CELEBRATION OF LOCAL CREATIVITY FOR MIAMI ART WEEK 2026
data.description:
From immersive installations and hands-on art experiences to live painting and art-inspired culinary offerings, the South Beach hotel puts local talent in the spotlight

MIAMI, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- At Kimpton Surfcomber Hotel, art isn't reserved for one week of the year. From its historic Art Deco roots to its ongoing collaborations with local artists, creativity is woven into the essence of the oceanfront South Beach hotel. This Miami Art Week, Surfcomber is building on that legacy with a special lineup of experiences celebrating the talent and artistic spirit of its local community.

From a striking new lobby installation to interactive art experiences at its newly renovated signature restaurant, The Social Club, and a colorful showcase at the Cabanas at its newly opened Solei Beach Club, the programming brings creativity to every corner of the property. Paired with imaginative culinary and cocktail offerings and a special shopping pop-up, the celebration invites guests and locals to experience art in unexpected ways against the backdrop of Surfcomber's idyllic oceanfront setting.

"Art has always been part of Surfcomber's identity, and our connection to Miami's creative community extends far beyond Art Week," said Mohan Koka, General Manager of Kimpton Surfcomber Hotel. "Over the years, we've had the privilege of working with some incredibly talented local artists, and we love finding new ways to bring their creativity into the guest experience. This year's celebration is all about building on those relationships, giving artists a platform to share their work and inviting visitors to experience a side of Miami's art scene they might not otherwise discover."

This year's programming brings together Miami-born artist Alex Nuñez, collage artist Kimberly Welbaum—whose cutmepasteme works have adorned the walls of The Social Club since its renovation—and Miami-based painter Jonathan Pedigo. Together, their distinct artistic styles will take center stage across the property, inviting guests to explore thought-provoking installations, get creative alongside the artists, witness live painting in action and even take home a limited-edition piece of Surfcomber's Art Week celebration.

A Closer Look at Surfcomber's Miami Art Week Programming

No Vacancy, Miami Beach: Alex Nuñez's You Cannot Step into the Same Ocean TwiceAs part of the City of Miami Beach's No Vacancy public art program, Surfcomber will welcome Miami-born artist Alex Nuñez for an immersive installation on display from November 12 through December 19. Titled You Cannot Step into the Same Ocean Twice, the exhibition transforms The Nook, the hotel's cozy lobby corner, into an otherworldly environment featuring printed aluminum palms, paintings and works on paper, anchored by an iridescent portal that shifts with the changing light. The installation invites visitors to experience a familiar coastal landscape through an entirely new lens, offering a moment of discovery just steps from the energy of South Beach.

A Celebration of Collage at The Social ClubFrom November 29 through December 7, Surfcomber's newly renovated signature restaurant, The Social Club, will become a playground for creativity in collaboration with Miami-based collage artist Kimberly Welbaum, the talent behind cutmepasteme. A fixture of The Social Club's artistic identity since its renovation, Welbaum's vibrant, layered works have become part of the restaurant's everyday atmosphere. For Miami Art Week, the hotel is taking that relationship beyond the walls, inviting guests to engage directly with the artist and her creative process through interactive installations, hands-on experiences and exclusive, limited-edition artwork.

  • Your Mark of Art: From November 29 through December 5, guests dining at The Social Club can add their own artistic flair to an interactive art experience led by Kimberly Welbaum. Through hand-cut fragments, color becomes a language for emotion. Together, individual feelings become one collective work of art. Guests are invited to browse a collection of colorful fragments, select the pieces that speak to them and contribute their own arrangement to the evolving artwork. Following Miami Art Week, Welbaum will carefully preserve and refine the individual contributions, bringing them together into a finished, signed original artwork—a one-of-a-kind creation shaped by the guests who helped bring it to life. Click HERE to reserve your table for your mark of art.
  • Cut, Paste & Cocktails: On December 5, from 3 to 5 p.m., Welbaum will lead an intimate collage workshop where guests can explore her signature techniques, create their own artwork and enjoy unlimited Sarti and Aperol Spritz cocktails alongside charcuterie. Participants will leave with their finished creations and a take-home art kit. Space is limited to 30 guests. Click HERE to purchase tickets.
  • A Piece of Art Week to Take Home: To commemorate the collaboration, Welbaum has created 200 individually signed, limited-edition 8-by-10-inch art prints exclusively for Surfcomber. These special keepsakes will be placed in guest rooms during Miami Art Week, offering visitors a chance to bring a piece of the hotel's artistic spirit home.

Flavor of Miami: Jonathan Pedigo at Solei Beach ClubFrom November 30 through December 7, the new Cabanas at Solei Beach Club will be transformed into a vibrant showcase of local artistry with Flavor of Miami, a collaboration with Miami-based artist Jonathan Pedigo and The Curation Department, a creative platform connecting artists with spaces and audiences through curated art experiences. Known for his bold use of color, expressive compositions and playful visual storytelling, Pedigo brings a distinctly energetic aesthetic to the oceanfront setting, with a selection of his works displayed throughout the cabanas alongside art-inspired cocktails handcrafted by Solei Beach Club's expert mixologists. Guests can explore the pieces at their own pace, with QR codes offering a closer look at the artist and the inspiration behind his work. Cabanas are available to rent through ResortPass.

On Friday, December 4, Pedigo will put an artistic spin on Surfcomber's signature Social Hour with a special live painting experience from 5 to 7 p.m., open to hotel guests and the public alike. Visitors can settle in with a drink in hand and watch as the artist transforms a blank canvas into an original work of art, bringing a little extra color and creativity to the hotel's beloved evening ritual—all against the backdrop of its idyllic oceanfront setting. For more details and to RSVP, click here.

The Blue Dynasty Experience: Where Art Meets the MenuFrom November 30 through December 7, The Social Club will take Miami Art Week indulgence to new heights with the introduction of the Blue Dynasty Experience, an extravagant, limited-time culinary creation from Executive Chef Gastón Javier. Inspired by Johnnie Walker Blue Label, the experience puts a luxurious spin on the classic burger, featuring American Wagyu, aged Alpine cheese, Blue Label bacon jam and winter black truffle, all nestled in a buttery brioche roll. Served alongside duck-fat pomme pavé finished with truffle sea salt and paired with a 2 oz pour of Johnnie Walker Blue Label, the $125 experience offers a decidedly decadent way to savor Miami Art Week.

A Touch of Sparkle: Kendra Scott Holiday Pop-UpRounding out Kimpton Surfcomber's Miami Art Week festivities with a fashionable flourish, jewelry and lifestyle brand Kendra Scott will bring its signature style to the hotel lobby for a special one-day shopping experience on Saturday, December 5, from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. Celebrating fashion as another form of creative expression, the pop-up invites guests and locals to explore and shop the brand's newest collection, offering the perfect opportunity to discover a statement piece of their own amid the week's artistic inspiration.

"Miami Art Week is an incredible time to explore the city, but we also wanted to create moments that invite people to slow down and enjoy the art in a more personal way," said Victoria Palacio, Marketing Manager of Kimpton Surfcomber Hotel. "There's something special about sitting down for a meal and realizing you can contribute to the artwork around you, or watching an artist bring a painting to life while you're enjoying the ocean breeze. Those are the kinds of experiences we hope people take away from their time at Surfcomber."

With 200 feet of oceanfront in the heart of South Beach, Kimpton Surfcomber Hotel offers an inviting escape from the whirlwind of Miami Art Week without missing a moment of the excitement. Between gallery hopping and art-filled afternoons, visitors can settle into the laid-back coastal atmosphere of the newly opened Solei Beach Club, inspired by the sun-drenched shores of Spain, or linger over South of France-inspired cuisine at the newly renovated The Social Club. Whether stopping in for a creative experience, gathering with friends over a leisurely meal or making a weekend of it, Surfcomber brings together the art, energy and easygoing spirit that make Miami Beach unlike anywhere else.

For more information on Surfcomber's Miami Art Week programming, visit surfcomber.com/hotels-on-collins-ave/art-basel-miami. For hotel reservations, visit surfcomber.com.

data.title: Canadian Energy Seen Well-Placed Amid Mideast Tensions — Market Talk
data.description: Canadian energy stocks will continue to benefit from a slow off-ramp from the U.S.-Iran conflict, RBC analysts say in a report. While the sector has been "whipsawed by headlines" around Middle East tensions this year, RBC expects oil prices to stay elevated, forecasting crude to average $88 a barrel over the next four quarters. "There is no easy off ramp to the conflict," the analysts noted, adding that they view "the recent repricing of geopolitical risks post midterms as premature." RBC remains overweight energy, noting the sector "continues to have the most positives" in its estimates, led by lower debt, high free-cash-flow yields and a supportive domestic policy backdrop. (adriano.marchese@wsj.com)
